sentences.text: The holotype, which is the specimen the species is based on, had an estimated body weight of around 821 grams.
This creature possessed significantly shorter arms than its closest relatives, and its humerus was shorter than its femur, implying it was incapable of flight.
Its teeth in the premaxilla are tightly packed, resembling troodontids and Anchiornis rather than Archaeopteryx.
The furcula of Yuezhuornis has an obtuse angle, similar to Anchiornis and non-avialan paravians.
The fossil was discovered in the summer of 2024 in the Nanyuan Formation near Yangyuan Village, Fujian Province, China.
The forelimb proportions are most similar to non-avialan paravians and flightless birds, while anatomical features support a terrestrial ecology.
It is debated whether Yuezhuornis was secondarily flightless or if flight evolved twice within Avialae.
Yuezhuornis is classified as an early member of Avialae and is the sister taxon to Zhengheornis within the clade Zhengheornithidae.
It diverged after Anchiornithidae and Archaeopteryx but before Baminornis within Avialae.
Yuezhuornis lived during the Late Jurassic, spanning from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian ages, approximately 150 million years ago at the boundary.
The Nanyuan Formation represents a primarily swamp-like depositional environment.
